newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Airlines oppose high fees at HK's new airport.
newsitem.headline: Airlines oppose high fees at HK's new airport.

text.p: Airlines are opposed to high fees at Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok, which is due to open in April 1998, and they may look for other locations in the region, a newspaper said on Saturday.

Gilbert Chow, the deputy chairman of the Board of Airline Representatives, was quoted by the South China Morning Post as saying the prospect of higher landing fees, parking fees and rents was an ominous sign for airlines.
Hong Kong's Airport Authority indicated two weeks ago that a range of fees could be doubled from present levels at Kai Tak international airport.

Chow, who heads airline industry negotiations on the new airport, said such increases could seriously affect the earnings of many carriers given the present trend of declining passenger yields and margins on many Asian routes.
He said return on investment for Hong Kong-based operators stood at between 2.0 percent and 9.0 percent and this could be quickly eroded by higher airport fees.

He said other regional hubs such as Macau's airport, which opened last November, Singapore, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, as well as Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Guangzhou in China were possible alternatives if Chek Lap Kok proved too costly.
Chow, who is also Hong Kong general manager for Northwest Airlines, criticised government pressure on the Airport Authority to produce immediate returns.
